chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Basir, from Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said:

Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not leave for people in their deeds anything except what He has assigned for them of reward and recompense, and He did not leave for them in them anything except what He has assigned for them of punishment and retribution. So if He wills, He rewards; if He wills, He punishes; if He wills, He pardons; if He wills, He forgives; if He wills, He gives; if He wills, He withholds. And it is not for people to have any say in it, but Allah, the Exalted, is the One who does what He wills.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between human deeds and divine will in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to elucidate the Shia doctrine of *Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (the middle position between absolute determinism and free will), affirming that while human agency initiates the deed, the final decree of reward or punishment rests solely with Allah’s sovereign will. This highlights the balance between human responsibility and divine grace, a cornerstone of Shia theological discourse on *Adl* (Divine Justice).
